content:
Let the black squares be the target set (flipping exactly these makes the board all white). Work over \(\mathbb F_2\).

For an \(n\times n\) board, define the 2D difference
\[
D_{i,j}=x_{i,j}+x_{i-1,j}+x_{i,j-1}+x_{i-1,j-1}
\]
with \(x=0\) outside the board.

- A rectangle flip contributes exactly four \(1\)'s in this difference array, at the rectangle’s four corners.
- For the checkerboard black-square set on an even \(n\), the difference array has
\[
n+n+n+(n-1)=4n-1
\]
nonzero entries.

Thus if \(k\) rectangles are used, we need
\[
4k\ge 4n-1,
\]
so \(k\ge n\). For \(n=98\), at least \(98\) moves are necessary.

Construction: flip all \(49\) odd rows and all \(49\) odd columns. This flips exactly the squares with odd row/column parity, i.e. exactly the black squares, making the board all white.

So the minimum number of moves is
\[
\boxed{98}.
\]
